title: Why 2.4 Million Answers Lost to 50,000
question: Why 2.4 Million Answers Lost to 50,000
hook: In 1936 the biggest poll in history — 2.4 million responses — predicted a landslide for the loser, while a poll fifty times smaller called the race right.
core_idea: Bias is a property of the estimator, not the sample size — a skewed frame gives a systematic offset, and more data only narrows the scatter around the wrong answer: convergence, with confidence, to the wrong value.
visual_object: a target where responses accumulate ever more tightly around an off-center point
exclusions: no ten-mechanism taxonomy, no formula beyond Bias = E[θ̂]−θ shown once, no inverse probability weighting
